slides.texte_overlay:
7 social hacks that feel like
cheating at a wedding
Find out one fun fact about the couple before you go. How they met, a funny story. It gives you the perfect opener with every stranger at your table: "How do you know them?"
Talk to the people at your table before the food arrives. Introduce yourself to everyone, not just your neighbour. By dessert, you'll have a whole table of new friends.
Dance at least once, even badly. The guy who stands at the edge all night looks stiff. The one who jumps in for one song, laughing, looks like the most fun person there.
Ask the older relatives about the couple. "What was she like as a kid?" Grandparents and uncles love telling stories, and you'll hear the best ones of the whole night.
Thank the parents of the couple before you leave. "Beautiful day, thank you for having me." Ten seconds, and you're the guest they'll remember with a smile.
Try this for 30 days before the wedding: five minutes a day of history, art or science. You'll have something fun to say to every stranger at every single table.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days before the wedding: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. You'll have something fun to say to every stranger at every table.

slides.texte_overlay: Write a short message in the guest book that's actually personal. One memory, one wish. It's the page they'll read again in twenty years, and it'll make them smile.
